what: W. P. Carey is a REIT that buys warehouses, factories and shops and leases them straight back to the companies that use them, on very long leases with rent increases written in.
customers: Mid-sized industrial and retail companies in the United States and Europe that prefer to free up the cash tied in their buildings.
money: rent from single-tenant industrial, warehouse and retail properties
self-storage, operating properties and investment management
moat: Leases that run for decades with contractual rent increases, many of them tied to inflation, which makes the income unusually predictable for a landlord.
risks: Rising interest rates make the dividend yield less attractive and refinancing more expensive
The exit from office property cut the dividend in 2024 and the shares have not recovered
$8.9B of debt against $155M of cash in a business that depends on continual refinancing
opportunities: Analysts see about 14% upside and the portfolio now leans toward warehouses rather than offices
Most leases carry rent increases tied to inflation, so the income rises without new investment
Revenue has held near $1.7B through the office exit, which suggests the remaining portfolio is stable
watch: Occupancy and how much new property is bought at what yield.
